title: Exercise and rate of incident falls
description:
Intervention: exercise-interventions. Comparator: trial-comparator. Outcome: incident-fall-rate.

Exercise versus contributing trial comparator arms: incidence rate ratio 0.85 (95% CI 0.75 to 0.96), 29 trials, 14,475 participants, longest follow-up 6 to 24 months. Heterogeneity I-squared = 82.7% (supplied AHRQ abstract). This estimate applies to incident fall rate, not the number of people who fall.

Recommendation grade B: The USPSTF recommends exercise interventions for community-dwelling adults aged 65 years or older at increased fall risk.

USPSTF assessed moderate certainty of a moderate net benefit for its recommendation. This is not a certainty rating assigned by this implementation to the individual pooled estimate.

Harms: About half of exercise trials reported harms. Minor musculoskeletal symptoms were most common; serious harms were rare, with exercise-associated wrist and hip fractures reported in separate trials. Sparse reporting limits certainty about harms.

Limitations: Interventions, baseline risks and follow-up varied. The evidence does not select one best exercise regimen. Lack of statistically significant fracture or mortality reductions does not establish no effect.
